tasks.short: Organize and write technical material to agreed structure, style, clarity, and terminology standards.

steps.what: Gather approved specifications, existing instructions, and reference material from the {DOCS}.
Choose the reader tasks, scope, sequence, and document outline.
Draft explanations and procedures using the content plan and source pack.

loop.input: Approved source pack, content plan, document template, and terminology base.
loop.output: Technical draft with source references and explicit information gaps.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, values, units, and source references; writer reviews meaning and procedure sequence.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section; unresolved facts return to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but varied source prose needs synthesis into reader instructions.

steps.what: Check technical accuracy, operating sequence, and safety instructions.
Apply terminology, heading, numbering, and formatting standards.
Resolve remaining issues and accept the manuscript for publication preparation.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles versioned sources from the {DOCS}, while templates and a bounded drafting loop produce source-linked sections. Configured checks produce a quality report in the {DOCS}; technical approval and manuscript acceptance remain separate human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source versions were scattered, templates covered only structure, and technical synthesis still required substantial writing.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building source connectors and document generators. Bounded drafting can work within an approved source pack.
tasks.still_hard: Sources may omit operating conditions. Correct-looking instructions still need technical validation, especially where mistakes could harm people.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what readers must accomplish and recognize when an apparently clear instruction is unsafe or incomplete.
tasks.altitude: The writer spends more time testing explanations with users and resolving source gaps. Technical approval and publication decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare accessible manual layouts from structured content.
reach.learn: Semantic headings, reusable page structures, and accessible tables.

evidence.claim: Acrolinx supports repeatable style checks and quality gates.
A trial found gains in professional writing; it did not establish technical-manual accuracy or safety.
Source assembly, templates, and bounded drafting can be combined; effort and remaining-time estimates are planning assumptions.

assumptions: A typical company uses the {DOCS} for drafting and technical review.
Time shares are illustrative, with document work dominant as the priors suggest.
Collection requires approved source locations and version identifiers.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; national rules determine any employee consultation.
unknowns: Which sources are authoritative and accessible?
Who approves safety instructions and final manuscripts?
Does the {DOCS} support templates, tracked changes, and configured quality checks?
Which confidentiality restrictions and consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which manual sections can be generated from structured specifications alone?
How often do drafts introduce unsupported conditions or omit prerequisites?
Can operators complete representative tasks using the generated instructions?
new_work: Review source references and unresolved information gaps.
Maintain templates, terminology, and source connectors.
Revalidate instructions when sources or drafting rules change.

tasks.short: Keep writing files, revision histories, and approved versions traceable and retrievable.

steps.what: Save the latest working file in the shared {DOCS}.
Update document identifiers, version labels, status, and source links.
Record revision dates, contributors, and change references in the revision log.
Confirm the approved version and mark previous versions as superseded.

tasks.design: Configure version history, required metadata, and approval states in the {DOCS}. Use that history as the revision log, and make superseding a version a controlled transition that preserves earlier records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Local copies and inconsistent naming weakened version history. Separate logs repeated information already stored with files.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document controls can often handle this through configuration. Small deterministic adapters can connect approval records where needed.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting legacy copies, unclear ownership, and inconsistent retention rules require cleanup and decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve disputed provenance and decide which version represents the approved technical position.

ambition.what: Self-service document lineage lookup for customer support staff

tasks.altitude: Routine saving and logging largely disappear, leaving short exception reviews and occasional record cleanup. Decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check that a manuscript uses the correct approved source version.
reach.learn: Document identifiers, approval states, and revision lineage.

evidence.claim: Version history, required metadata, and approval states are established document-management capabilities.
A separate revision log can be removed when native history captures the required fields; estimates require local validation.

assumptions: The {DOCS} holds most working files, although some copies still require reconciliation.
Required change references can link to review records without model-generated summaries.
Superseding a version preserves it; deletion is outside this design.
GDPR applies to contributor records. National rules may require consultation if logging changes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Does native history meet contractual and retention requirements?
How many uncontrolled copies and conflicting identifiers exist?
Which metadata can be inherited reliably?
Who may change approval states and record access?
research_questions: Can native history replace all required revision-log fields?
Can representative users retrieve the approved version and its review evidence?
What exceptions remain after a small legacy-document migration?
new_work: Resolve missing identifiers and conflicting versions.
Maintain metadata rules, permissions, and approval transitions.
Check broken source links and periodically test retrieval.

tasks.short: Edit colleagues' technical material for consistency, clarity, and accurate meaning.

steps.what: Collect the contributor draft, references, and editing brief through the {EMAIL}.
Check spelling, terminology, references, and house-style compliance.
Restructure unclear passages and propose edits while preserving technical meaning.

loop.input: Contributor draft, source pack, style rules, and quality report.
loop.output: Tracked edits with reasons and queries for ambiguous technical statements.
loop.check: Compare numbers, units, identifiers, warnings, and conditions; writer reviews semantic changes.
loop.stop: One edit pass and one repair pass per section; unresolved meaning becomes an author query.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules identify standard violations but cannot reliably restructure varied prose while preserving its intended meaning.

steps.what: Discuss ambiguous statements and confirm corrections to technical meaning.
Accept agreed edits and hand over the approved manuscript.

tasks.design: A submission flow in the {WORKFLOW} places drafts and references in the {DOCS}, where configured checks run first. A bounded editing loop proposes tracked changes and author queries; technical corrections and final acceptance receive their respective human approvals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rule checkers handled surface consistency, while mixed-quality drafts and ambiguous meaning still required extensive manual editing.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured checks can be combined with bounded rewriting and deterministic comparisons of protected technical values.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent rewrite can change a qualification, warning, or operating condition. Conflicting expert opinions still need resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether clearer wording preserves the author's intended technical claim and the reader's ability to act safely.
tasks.altitude: The writer reviews proposed changes and spends more time resolving meaning with contributors. Editorial and technical approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Prepare translation updates from approved technical changes.
reach.learn: Term-base structure, translation context, and stable segment identifiers.

evidence.claim: LanguageTool checks spelling, grammar, punctuation, and style.
Acrolinx provides house-style scoring and quality gates.
A vendor case reports fewer translation edits; it does not establish savings for this workflow.
Protected-value comparisons and tracked model edits can support human editing; remaining-time estimates are unvalidated.

assumptions: Drafts commonly arrive through the {EMAIL}, while most editing happens in the {DOCS}.
Style rules and approved terminology can be separated from technical meaning decisions.
The high automation prior is moderated because semantic changes still require review.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant; any employee consultation follows national rules.
unknowns: Which edits may be accepted without technical reapproval?
Are tracked changes preserved across the actual document formats?
Which values, warnings, and terms require exact preservation?
Can the source material be processed within approved confidentiality controls?
research_questions: Which edit categories are safe for deterministic correction?
How often do proposed rewrites alter technical meaning?
Do change packs reduce clarification requests from translators?
new_work: Review semantic changes and resolve author queries.
Maintain style rules, protected terms, and edit examples.
Investigate recurring false positives and missed technical changes.

tasks.short: Assess field developments and decide which published materials need revision or replacement.

steps.what: Collect release notes, standards notices, and relevant field publications.
Compare developments with published instructions and identify potentially affected sections.

loop.input: New source passages and published sections selected by identifiers, versions, and terminology.
loop.output: Candidate affected sections with paired source passages and proposed impact categories.
loop.check: Require valid source and section references; writer reviews relevance and samples unmatched developments.
loop.stop: One assessment and one repair pass per source item; uncertain matches enter the review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact identifiers handle explicit links, but changes expressed in different language need semantic comparison.

steps.what: Discuss applicability, technical consequences, and urgency with the writer.
Decide whether to revise, create new material, or take no action.
Write the revision brief with affected sections, sources, and acceptance criteria.
Create revision work items and link the supporting brief in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collects approved change sources and matches explicit identifiers against the document register in the {DOCS}. A bounded comparison loop proposes an impact map; human decisions feed template-generated revision briefs and linked work items in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Developments and published sections lacked reliable links. Keyword searches missed changes expressed through different terminology.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic collection and version matching narrow the material needing semantic comparison. Bounded models can propose evidence-linked matches for review.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete coverage can hide an important development. Applicability, urgency, safety implications, and competing priorities remain judgments.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when a development changes real operating practice and when apparent novelty needs no documentation change.
tasks.altitude: The writer can run a short weekly impact review instead of periodically rebuilding the evidence. Revision, safety, and release decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess which field developments affect customer information needs.
reach.learn: Source reliability, trend validation, and customer-segment relevance.

evidence.claim: Full Fact AI identifies checkable claims and matches repeated claims; this is adjacent to document-impact matching.
Archive question-answering is being tested in publishing; the digest provides no technical-manual impact-analysis case.
Identifier matching, bounded semantic comparison, and decision-driven brief generation form a plausible design requiring local validation.

assumptions: The company maintains identifiable published versions and an agreed source watchlist.
Revision decisions capture reasons and acceptance criteria in structured fields.
Collection automates known sources; it does not guarantee discovery of every relevant development.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply as relevant. Source access rights and national consultation rules must be respected.
Build ranges are working-day estimates; external access and consultation may take longer in elapsed time.
unknowns: Which sources and jurisdictions must the watchlist cover?
Are product versions linked to document sections?
Who decides urgent safety updates and documentation priorities?
Can external publications be retrieved and processed under existing access rights?
What cadence can technical reviewers support?
research_questions: Does retrospective testing recover known revision-triggering developments?
Which unmatched notices reveal gaps in the watchlist or document register?
Does weekly triage improve revision timeliness without creating an unmanageable backlog?
new_work: Maintain source coverage, identifiers, and document mappings.
Review uncertain matches and sample apparently unaffected documents.
Record missed developments and adjust matching rules.
Reconcile generated work items with backlog capacity.

role.altitude: The technical writer spends less time assembling files, applying routine standards, and copying revision details. More of the week goes to reader testing, technical ambiguity, and revision priorities; existing approval rights remain unchanged.
reach: Desktop publishing: accessible layouts from structured manuscripts.
Translation: source-linked change packs and terminology context.
Market research: evidence-based assessment of changing reader needs.
skills_to_grow: Rule-based quality checks and exception handling
Evaluation of model edits for semantic changes
Reader testing and technical risk assessment
role.ambitious_version: Provide version-specific operator guides and a weekly documentation-impact service, supported by traceable sources and explicit technical approvals.
